blocks.content: Create a ping check to learn whether a host responds from different locations. For website availability or page content, use an HTTP or browser check instead.
First, open Synthetic Monitoring:
Click **Testing & synthetics** in the main menu.
blocks.tooltip: Open the area containing availability and performance testing tools.

blocks.content: Click **Synthetics**.
blocks.tooltip: Open the checks and results for this stack.

whenTrue.content: Click **Get started** if this stack has not used Synthetic Monitoring before. Ask an administrator to complete this one-time setup.
whenTrue.tooltip: An administrator only needs to initialize this service once per stack.

blocks.content: Once Synthetic Monitoring is open, you're ready to create a check.
Choose a target and probe locations for your first check. You need the Editor or Admin role.
Click **Create new check**.
blocks.tooltip: Choose a check type based on what you need to test.

blocks.content: Click **API Endpoint**. Ping lives here, alongside HTTP, DNS, and TCP checks.
blocks.tooltip: This editor supports HTTP, ping, DNS, TCP, and traceroute checks.

blocks.content: Enter a descriptive **Job name**, such as `my-website-uptime`.
blocks.formHint: Enter a descriptive name for your application or check.
blocks.tooltip: This name becomes the job label used to find the check in metrics and logs.

blocks.content: Under **Request type**, click **Ping** to send a network packet and wait for a response.
blocks.tooltip: Ping tests whether a host responds to network packets; it does not check page content or HTTP responses.

blocks.content: Enter your hostname or IP address, such as `grafana.com`.
blocks.formHint: Enter a hostname or IP address, without a URL scheme or path.
blocks.tooltip: Use only the host, without https:// or a path; some hosts block ping even when their website is healthy.

blocks.content: Click **Execution** to choose probe locations and a schedule.
blocks.tooltip: Each selected location runs the check independently at the frequency you choose.

blocks.content: Select at least one online probe near your users. Review **Frequency** and the estimated usage before saving; more probes and more frequent checks generate more usage.
Click **Save** to start the check and open its dashboard.
blocks.tooltip: Review the target, selected probes, and estimated usage before saving.

blocks.content: Your check is live. Probes are already pinging the target from the locations you picked.
Finally, read the results on the dashboard that just opened:
**Uptime** is the percentage of checks that succeeded. Give it a few minutes to populate, and refresh if it's empty.
blocks.tooltip: A low value means one or more probe locations could not reach the target.

blocks.content: **Reachability** shows how often the target responds, per probe location.
blocks.tooltip: Compare locations to distinguish a widespread outage from a regional network problem.

blocks.content: **Average latency** shows how long the response takes from each location. Distance shows up here.
blocks.tooltip: Compare locations over the same time range; longer network paths usually take more time.

blocks.content: You have continuous, outside-in monitoring of your site, and it keeps running after you close this browser.

Note: each probe runs the check separately, so a check's usage is its frequency multiplied by its probe count. A check that runs every minute from five probes costs five times the executions of the same check from one probe. Give each check the frequency and probe count its target actually needs, not the maximum.
